skill.name: peak-setup
skill.description: Move a repository's GitHub Actions jobs to Peak runners when the user requests Peak setup or faster CI. Run the Peak CLI in agent mode, relay sign-in details, and return the pull request link.
skill.summary: Configure GitHub Actions to use Peak runners and report the resulting pull request.
skill.author: peakinc

security_audit.summary: All 25 external-command alerts are false positives because they match Markdown backticks and documented command text, not executable Ruby or shell code. The two URL alerts are also false positives because they are fixed documentation links; however, the instructions introduce supply-chain and workflow-disclosure risks through mutable npx packages and remote workflow processing.

remediation.issue: The setup commands use mutable @latest package versions with npx -y, allowing a future package release to execute in the repository context.
remediation.suggestion: Pin @peakinc/init and @peakinc/wizard to reviewed versions, verify package provenance and integrity, and require explicit confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: The wizard sends selected workflow files to Peak over a network connection, which may disclose repository configuration or proprietary CI logic.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact files and data transferred, obtain explicit user consent, minimize the transmitted scope, and provide a local-only fallback for sensitive repositories.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Remote Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The instructions tell the agent to run npx -y with @peakinc/init@latest and @peakinc/wizard@latest in the repository. A future package release can execute with repository access before the user reviews a pull request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands explicitly use npx -y and mutable @latest package tags, which directly establishes unattended remote package execution in the repository context.

semantic_findings.title: Workflow File Disclosure to External Service
semantic_findings.description: The wizard path states that selected workflow files are sent to Peak over a network connection. This can disclose proprietary CI logic or configuration to an external service without a documented data review or local-only option.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly describes transmitting workflow files to Peak, but it provides no evidence that those files contain secrets or that the transfer is malicious; the concern is disclosure and consent.

content.user_title: Move CI Jobs to Peak Runners
content.value_statement: Teams need a faster GitHub Actions runner setup without manually editing every workflow. This skill runs the Peak workflow, guides authentication, and reports the proposed changes for review.
actual_capabilities: Checks repository, GitHub remote, Node version, and organization ownership prerequisites.
Runs the Peak initialization CLI with structured JSON output.
Relays authorization links, user codes, pull request links, and failure details.
Explains jobs that require the Peak wizard because they use complex runner configurations.
Provides a manual runs-on replacement when the CLI commands cannot run.
Describes how to undo the branch created by the initialization command.
limitations: The setup requires a GitHub organization owner and does not support personal accounts.
Node 22.13 or newer must be installed in the repository environment.
The CLI and wizard depend on network access and third-party Peak packages.
The skill does not merge pull requests or independently verify the resulting CI run.

use_cases.title: Migrate a GitHub Actions repository
use_cases.description: Set up Peak runners across eligible workflow jobs and return a pull request for the repository owner to review.

use_cases.title: Investigate jobs needing translation
use_cases.description: Identify matrix jobs, operating system legs, and runner expressions that require the Peak wizard or manual handling.

use_cases.title: Prepare a cautious runner transition
use_cases.description: Apply the runner change through a pull request, preserve the existing CI, and explain the steps for validation and rollback.

prompt_templates.title: Start Peak setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Peak in this repository. Check the prerequisites first, run the standard initialization flow, and report the pull request link.

prompt_templates.title: Review the migration plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository for Peak setup readiness. Summarize eligible jobs, blocked jobs, required authentication, and the expected workflow change before running the CLI.

prompt_templates.title: Handle hard jobs
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Peak setup flow and handle jobs that use matrices, expressions, or non-Linux runners. Report translated jobs, skipped jobs, reasons, and the pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Use a controlled fallback
prompt_templates.prompt: If Peak initialization cannot run, identify each eligible GitHub Actions job, propose the exact runs-on migration, preserve all other workflow content, and prepare the changes for review.

output_examples.input: Set up Peak for this GitHub repository.
output_examples.output: Prerequisites passed. Peak authentication is required. Open the provided sign-in link and approve access. The CLI will return a pull request after updating eligible runner labels.

output_examples.input: Why were some jobs not moved to Peak?
output: The plan identified jobs with matrix or runner expression complexity.
Those jobs require the Peak wizard or manual review.
The report includes each skipped job and its reason.

output_examples.input: The CLI cannot run. What should I do?
output_examples.output: Use the manual fallback for eligible workflow jobs: change only the runs-on value, open a pull request, and leave the existing CI steps unchanged.

best_practices: Review the generated pull request before merging and confirm every runner change.
Keep the existing CI until the first successful Peak run validates the migration.
Never expose PEAK_TOKEN or other credentials in logs, prompts, or pull request text.
anti_patterns: Do not merge the pull request automatically.
Do not edit workflow steps or unrelated settings during runner migration.
Do not run the setup without reviewing the package source, version, and data-transfer behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill change?
faq.answer: It changes eligible GitHub Actions runner assignments and creates a pull request. It should leave other workflow content unchanged.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: You need to be an owner of the GitHub organization. Personal accounts are not supported by the documented workflow.

faq.question: Which Node version is required?
faq.answer: The instructions require Node 22.13 or newer.

faq.question: Will the skill merge my pull request?
faq.answer: No. It reports the pull request and leaves the merge decision to you.

faq.question: What happens to complex jobs?
faq.answer: Jobs with matrix, operating system, or runner expression complexity may be sent through the Peak wizard or left for manual review.

faq.question: Can I undo the setup?
faq.answer: The documented undo command removes the branch created by initialization. Review its effect before running it.
